__comment__: POSITION IS [0,0,0] AND MUST STAY THAT WAY.
A bone animation's position is applied in the bone's OWN ROTATED frame, so a
large Y lift combined with a rotation slides the model sideways instead of
straight up — that is what threw the handset off to one side of the arm and
left the playing card lying on the ground.
The hand height is baked into the GEOMETRY instead, exactly the way Microsoft's
wrench sample does it: every held .geo.json has its cubes shifted so the model's
centre sits at y=22 (about hand height) with the bone pivot at [0,22,0].
Geometry coordinates are never rotated, so that offset is stable. This file only
rotates and scales, about a pivot that is already on the hand.
If a model needs to sit higher or lower, move the CUBES in its .geo.json.
Do not reintroduce a position offset here.
